$comment: AUTHORED, not produced by any binding — this golden states esm-spec §6.3.1 rather than recording what an implementation happens to do. `wf`, `ws` and `wb` are the three unknowns the category exists for: all three are DEFINED by an equation whose LHS names them through an index, so all three are observed. `im` is the control that must stay algebraic, `u` and `v` the control that must stay ODE states even though their derivative LHSs wear the same `aggregate` shell, and `sc` the rank-0 control §6.3.1 says the arrayed ones must match. Lists are sorted lexicographically by UTF-8 code point.

flatten_buckets.$comment: esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5 step 4's flattened-representation buckets for this same fixture, AUTHORED against that table rather than minted by a binding. The two maps are NOT a partition: `state_variables` is the SOLVED-FOR VECTOR ("Differential unknowns …, PLUS `algebraic_variables`, PLUS any arrayed observed that materializes into a buffer") and `observed_variables` is the §6.3.1 CLASSIFICATION ("Unknowns DEFINED by an equation, bare-LHS or indexed-LHS … an arrayed observed materializes into a buffer and IS [in state_variables]"). So `wf`, `ws` and `wb` are in BOTH; `sc` — a SCALAR observed, "eliminated by substitution and … NOT in state_variables" — is in `observed_variables` only; and `im` is in `state_variables` and `algebraic_variables` at once, the dual membership the same table already requires of an algebraic unknown ("A subset of state_variables — a DAE solves for them"). Names are dot-namespaced and every list is in DOCUMENT order, which step 4 makes normative — this is the one golden here that is NOT sorted. Issue #270.
